headline.technical: S&P 500 rose 4.73% on 2026-11-23 as Nvidia surged 31.5% after Huang's reinstatement (Mint); Asia followed (TAIEX 8.99%, KOSPI 6.32%) while Europe slipped and Nasdaq futures fell (WSJ).
headline.layman: Tech shares bounced hard after Nvidia brought back its founder as boss. The US market jumped and Asia followed, but Europe slipped and US futures edged down.

global.title: AI-led rebound after the selloff, but doubts linger

status.technical: S&P 500 closed 7237.17 on 2026-11-23, up 4.73% in a day (1-day move z-score 4.32), though still -2.42% over 5d. Mint reported Nvidia rose 31.5% after its board reinstated Jensen Huang. VIX closed at 28.59. WSJ reported Nasdaq futures fell as questions lingered over the AI trade.
status.layman: The S&P 500, a gauge of big US companies, jumped 4.73% on Monday after Nvidia's board brought back Jensen Huang as boss. Mint reported Nvidia shares rose 31.5%. The VIX, a 'fear gauge', is at 28.59.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Nomura said mechanical buying helped the rally. If the rebound leans on forced flows rather than new demand, it may fade. Julius Baer called the recent AI selloff a realignment of expectations and valuations, not a broken investment cycle (WSJ).
consequence.layman: Bloomberg reported Nomura saw some automatic, forced buying in the rally. If so, the jump may not mean buyers changed their minds. Julius Baer called the AI selloff a reset of expectations, not a broken boom.

impact.technical: WSJ ran a headline saying the dollar's fortunes are closely linked to the AI trade, and Mint quoted experts saying an AI revival may jeopardize foreign money flowing into Indian stocks. The notes say little about other effects, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: A WSJ headline says the dollar moves closely with the AI trade. Experts quoted by Mint said a stronger AI trade could pull money away from India. Beyond that, the notes say little.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 51% of 192 times and the next 5 days rose 54% of 192 times (median 0.24%). Look-alike days: next 5 days rose 4 of 5 times (median 2.84%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big up days like this, the S&P 500 rose the next day 51% of the time, close to a coin flip. Over the next 5 days it rose 54% of the time.

status.technical: Nasdaq Composite rose 6.51% (close 24089.56), Dow 3.01% and Russell 2000 3.40% on 2026-11-23. Bovespa fell -0.95% (1m -20.19%); Bloomberg reported Brazil's real hit a 19-month low as a post-election selloff deepened.
status.layman: US stocks surged on Monday: the Nasdaq rose 6.51% and the Dow 3.01%. Brazil went the other way. The Bovespa slipped 0.95%, and Bloomberg said Brazil's currency hit a 19-month low after the election.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Brazil analysts raised 2027 key-rate and inflation forecasts for a second straight week on fiscal concerns. If fiscal worries persist, rate expectations may stay high. Reuters reported a primary surplus target of up to 2% of GDP.
consequence.layman: Bloomberg reported Brazilian economists raised forecasts for interest rates and inflation for a second week in a row. If worries about government spending continue, borrowing costs could stay high.

impact.technical: Bloomberg reported Mexico's economy grew at its fastest annual pace since 2023 in Q3 on strong exports; the IPC rose 1.06% on the day. The notes say little about other Americas effects, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: Bloomberg said Mexico's economy grew at its fastest yearly pace since 2023, helped by exports. Mexico's main index rose 1.06%. The notes say little about other effects.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 53% of 196 times and the next 5 days rose 53% of 196 times (10th-90th pct -4.12% to 3.18%). Bovespa after ordinary days: next 5 days rose 52% of 833 times.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big Nasdaq jumps, it rose the next day 53% of the time and over the next 5 days 53% of the time, with a wide range of outcomes (-4.12% to 3.18%).

status.layman: European markets mostly slipped on Tuesday: Germany's DAX fell 0.72% and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.66%. Morningstar reported chip shares fell once the Nvidia boost faded.

consequence.technical: SCMP reported the Dutch foreign minister is visiting China as the Nvidia saga revives a US push for tougher ASML curbs. If curbs tighten, ASML's China sales could be affected; some analysts said the visit could strengthen the Dutch case.
consequence.layman: SCMP reported the Dutch foreign minister is going to China while the US pushes for tougher limits on ASML's sales there. If the limits tighten, ASML's China business could suffer.

drivers.title: Nvidia's Huang reinstated; AI trade rebounds

status.technical: Mint reported Nvidia's board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, president and board member, triggering a 31.5% share-price surge. Nvidia rose +31.48% (1d) and +5.71% (5d). CNBC reported analysts said Huang is 'too big to fire', putting governance in focus.
status.layman: Mint reported Nvidia's board brought back co-founder Jensen Huang as boss and the shares jumped 31.5%. CNBC reported analysts say the company relies heavily on him, which puts its board under scrutiny.

consequence.technical: CNBC said questions remain over the board's reversal and Trump's involvement. If governance doubts or export limits weigh, the rebound could stall; Mint said brokerages turned more positive but flagged export restrictions, China exposure and AI spending uncertainty.
consequence.layman: Questions remain about why the board changed course. If worries about governance or export limits grow, the rebound could stall. Mint said brokers turned more positive but still flagged those risks.

impact.technical: Mint said the rally lifted other AI-related stocks and the Nasdaq. SCMP reported Ark Investment's Cathie Wood dumped almost US$107 million of Nvidia shares before the rally.
impact.layman: Mint said the rally lifted other AI stocks and the Nasdaq. SCMP reported Cathie Wood's fund sold almost US$107 million of Nvidia shares just before the jump.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 53% of 196 times. Look-alike days: next 21 days rose 3 of 5 times (median 1.35%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after big Nasdaq jumps, the next day was up 53% of the time. In 5 similar past cases, 3 were higher a month later.

drivers.title: Oil falls on US-Iran diplomacy, Hormuz risk remains

status.technical: Brent closed 86.72 (1d -2.97%, 1m -25.12%). Bloomberg reported oil held its decline on signs of continuing US-Iran diplomacy; CNBC reported Iran said three tankers hit mines in Hormuz despite US escort.
status.layman: Brent oil closed at 86.72, down 2.97% on the day. Bloomberg said oil stayed lower as US-Iran talks seemed to continue, while CNBC reported Iran said three tankers hit mines in Hormuz.

consequence.technical: Business Standard reported traders weighing rising supply against persistent shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz. If diplomacy holds, oil could stay lower; if Hormuz incidents escalate, that supply risk could return.
consequence.layman: Traders are weighing more supply against shipping dangers in the Strait of Hormuz, Business Standard said. If talks hold, oil could stay cheaper. More shipping incidents could push it back up.

impact.technical: Business Standard said the Sensex's November gain of nearly 11% came amid lower crude prices, among other factors. Bloomberg reported Bahrain's slumping economy is under pressure from Iranian bombardments.
impact.layman: Business Standard said India's market rose nearly 11% in November partly because oil got cheaper. Bloomberg said Bahrain's weak economy is strained by Iranian attacks.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days Brent's next day rose 53% of 847 times and the next 5 days rose 51% of 844 times.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions: after ordinary days, Brent rose the next day 53% of the time, and over 5 days 51% of the time.

drivers.title: US inflation worries and Treasury yields

status.technical: US 10-year yield closed 4.92 on 2026-11-23 (1d 0.12%, 5d -3.96%). CNBC reported yields steadied after an inflation warning from New York Fed's Williams, with a 5-year auction awaited; Investing.com ran a headline that inflation worries grow over Warsh's Fed.
status.layman: The US 10-year yield, a key borrowing-cost benchmark, closed at 4.92. CNBC reported yields held steady after New York Fed's Williams warned about inflation, ahead of a 5-year bond auction.

consequence.technical: If inflation worries persist, as the Williams warning suggests, yields may stay elevated. Russell 2000 daily moves correlated -0.3 with the 10-year yield over the past year, so higher yields have tended to coincide with weaker small caps.
consequence.layman: If inflation worries stick, borrowing costs may stay high. Over the past year, small US stocks tended to fall on days when yields rose (correlation -0.3).

impact.technical: The notes give only headlines on this theme and do not describe who is affected, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: The notes only give headlines here and don't say who is affected, so there is little to add.

consequence.layman: If the pause ends after January, China's leverage over supplies could come back. The notes only cover the extension itself.
